title.narrative: Life-Saving IDP and Famine Response in North Darfur State: Addressing Urgent Needs in Dar Al-Salam and Al-Fasher

description.narrative: ltpgtRelief International and its partners aim to address the health, nutrition, and protection needs of individuals in Dar el Salam and El Fasher localities, including the Zamzam IDP camp, which are currently facing famine conditions. The project seeks to reach individuals by improving access to healthcare, nutrition, WASH, and protection services. The project will strengthen primary healthcare, including emergency trauma response and outbreak management, in collaboration with the State Ministry of Health (SMoH), addressing diseases such as measles, malaria, and cholera. Integrated Community Case Management (ICCM) will be implemented to ensure early diagnosis and treatment of common diseases at the community level, while secondary healthcare services, including the Dar El Salam and El Fasher Maternity Hospitals and stabilization centers in Zamzam and Dar El Salam, will receive support to ensure continuity of care. Through this project, RI and its partners are planning to reach 148,996 beneficiaries with health services and 53,579 with nutrition activities. ltbrgtIn addition to health and nutrition services, protection activities will be integrated to meet the needs of vulnerable populations, particularly women and girls. RI will establish safe spaces for women and girls and will enhance Sexual and Gender-Based Violence (SGBV) and Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) services. Structured MHPSS services will also be provided to distressed children, and parenting programs will target caregivers to ensure a protective environment for children. Specialized case management services will be offered to at-risk children and GBV survivors. The project will also strengthen community-based protection networks (CBPNs) to enhance the safety and resilience of vulnerable populations, using a community-based and gender-sensitive approach.ltbrgtSudan hosts over 10.8 million internally displaced persons (IDPs) and 2.3 million refugees in neighboring countries. In areas like Zamzam camp, trapped populations face severe barriers to accessing safer areas due to conflict and high travel costs. The escalation of conflict in North Darfur, particularly in crop-producing areas during harvest season, has led to widespread food shortages, increased malnutrition, and famine. El Fasher and Dar El Salam localities currently have some of the highest GAM rates in Sudan, at 21.6% and 29.7%, respectively. Both localities are classified under IPC 4, with famine declared in Zamzam IDP camp in El Fasher. Additionally, the flooding season has heightened the risk of waterborne diseases. The destruction of health facilities, lack of medical supplies, and strained healthcare services in IDP areas have caused rising mortality rates, particularly among children. The lack of clean water, sanitation, and hygiene services further exacerbates the spread of preventable diseases among displaced populations. ltbrgtRI will integrate conflict sensitivity into all project activities, ensuring interventions are adapted to the volatile environment and align with the "do no harm" principle. This approach includes conducting conflict analyses, engaging communities, ensuring transparent beneficiary selection, and performing regular risk assessments. By working closely with communities and local authorities, RI will promote peace and stability while providing timely assistance to those in need. Staff training, monitoring and evaluation, feedback mechanisms, and flexible programming will ensure the delivery of health, nutrition, and protection services without worsening local tensions.ltbrgtlt/pgt
